title: Latency flare hunt protocol and sampling checklist
content:
Purpose and when to use this:
This is a lightweight playbook for investigating short-duration latency spikes ("flares") that appear in production or in canaries. It combines a high-signal sampling protocol with dashboard checks and a minimal bisect checklist so you can form a hypothesis in < 60 minutes and collect artifacts for a longer root cause hunt. Use for: sudden 95/99th percentile jumps, microburst alerts, and noisy canary deltas that don't immediately reproduce in load tests.

Quick summary steps (10–60m):
1) Signal validation (0–5m)
  - Confirm the alert source (Grafana panel, SLO sentinel, oncall). Timestamp(s) and sample IDs.
  - Snapshot the dashboard: save PNG and note exact query time ranges.
  - Check correlated signals: host CPU/GPU usage, network errors, kvcache eviction rate, qps drop.

2) Reduce noise and isolate slices (5–15m)
  - Restrict timeframe to spike window +/- 2m. Compare baseline window of same hour previous day.
  - Filter for route/model/tenant: does spike show across all routes or a single route? If single route, tag the alert and treat as application-level.
  - If in canary: compare canary vs production traffic for identical request traces (sample ids).

3) Rapid artifact grab (5–20m)
  - Capture 1–3 flamegraphs from the affected hosts/gpus. Use 10s pprof or eBPF sampling during a live window. Command examples (on SRE jump host):
      curl -sS "http://perf-agent:9090/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=10" > flare-pprof-10s.pb.gz
      go tool pprof -http=:8081 flare-pprof-10s.pb.gz
  - Export per-request traces (trace-id header values). Use trace storage query by timestamp and service: e.g.,
      SELECT * FROM traces WHERE service='inference' AND timestamp BETWEEN ts0 AND ts1 LIMIT 200
  - Pull KV cache stats and eviction logs for the same hosts.
  - Pull model runtime counters: kernel selection counts, quantization path hits, batch sizes.

4) Quick bisect heuristic (10–30m)
  - Time-based bisect: is there a deploy, config change, or infra event near window? Check PR merges, infra autoscaler events, and node pool rotations.
  - Canary vs prod split: if only canary is bad, evaluate traffic differences (sample weights, synthetic vs user, request shapes). If only prod is bad, look for rate or regional routing changes.
  - Config axis: batching thresholds, adaptive_batch toggles, kvcache size changes, new kernel feature flags. Revert candidates are prioritized by blast radius.

5) Decide mitigation path (5–15m)
  - If spike is limited to canary: pause canary rollout or scale canary back to 0.
  - If spike is in prod and tied to recent deploy: rollback or trigger a gradual rollback by shifting traffic if we have traffic splitting.
  - If spike is infra (e.g., node GC, preemption): schedule node replacement and enable safe-fallback routes.

Sampling protocol (to maximize signal-to-noise during flares)
- Aim: collect deterministic, minimal artifacts with low overhead.
- Always capture: 10s pprof flamegraph, 1s-resolution latency histogram for 5 minutes, 100 request traces sampled from high-latency tail.
- Sampling rules: prioritize traces with latency > p95 during flare and with identical model+route+input-shape. Tag traces with model-version and quantization profile.
- Storage: upload artifacts to /artifacts/latency-flares/<incident-id>/ with metadata.json containing the queries used and Grafana PNGs.

Dashboard checklist (which panels to open)
- Global: 1m/5m p99 latency, request rate, error rate, throughput per region.
- Node-level: GPU utilization, PCIe transfers, GPU SM stalls, memory copy latency, OOM events.
- Runtime-level: batch size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, kernel-fallback counts, slow-path execution time.
- Tracing: waterfall view for sampled traces, token path latency split (embedding->encode->decode).
- Canary comparison panel: side-by-side p95/p99 and token per-second curves.

Representative queries and metrics to run (Grafana/PromQL examples)
- p99 latency (api handler): sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le="0.5",route=~".*infer.*"}[5m])) by (le)
- kvcache eviction rate: increase(kvcache_evictions_total[10m]) / increase(kvcache_requests_total[10m])
- kernel fallback count: increase(runtime_kernel_fallbacks_total[15m])
- per-model batch size histogram: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(model_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le,model))

Bisect checklist (artifact-driven)
- Confirm reproducibility in canary with synthetic workload matching sample trace. If reproducible, run narrow A/B with the suspected commit/flag.
- If not reproducible, collect longer-term traces and correlate with distributed events (network blips, storage latency).
- Use snapshot comparison tool: take perf-snapshot pre/post and run diff to surface token-level regressions.

What to collect for postmortem (minimum):
- Incident id and timeline (alerts, mitigation actions, time to mitigate).
- Grafana snapshots and exact PromQL queries.
- 3 flamegraphs (worst host, median host, canary host).
- 100 sampled trace ids + trace JSONs.
- Node events (kube events, preemptions, autoscaler logs).
- Any suspect PRs/feature flags with links.

Decision matrix (quick):
- If artifact shows kernel fallback spikes -> mark as "runtime fallback" and set priority to P1, require kernel-level instrumentation ticket.
- If KV cache eviction correlated -> prioritize cache tuning + temporary cache-size increase as mitigation.
- If batch size collapsed -> investigate admission control throttle changes or upstream traffic shaping.
- If GPU stalls or PCIe spikes -> SRE oncall to check noisy neighbors / instance health and consider draining nodes.

Playbook snippets and commands
- Collect flamegraph from n hosts in parallel:
    for h in host1 host2 host3; do ssh $h "curl -sS http://localhost:9090/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=10" > /tmp/$h-pprof.pb.gz & done; wait
- Query traces by latency:
    curl -sS "https://traces.redwood.ai/api/traces?service=inference&minDurationMs=200&start=$TS0&end=$TS1" > traces.json
- Pull KV cache telemetry for model X:
    kubectl logs deployment/model-serving --since=10m -l model=x | jq '.kvcache' > kvcache.log

Notes on avoiding false positives
- Temporary spikes during traffic surge or A/B experiment ramping are common; always cross-check with deployment timelines and experiments board.
- Synthetic tests can mask production variability if they use homogeneous inputs; always compare input-shape distributions.

Follow-ups and improvement ideas
- Add an automatic flare collector that runs the sampling protocol automatically for any p99 jump > 40% lasting > 60s.
- Enrich canary traffic with seeded high-variance inputs to catch quantization/kernel regressions earlier.
- Instrument token-path level timing in the runtime to get finer-grained attribution.

Incident template (copy/paste for postmortems)
- Title: "INCIDENT: latency flare - <route/model> - <date>"
- Summary: 1–2 sentence summary of what happened and user impact.
- Timeline: bullet list of events with ISO timestamps.
- Root cause hypothesis: short paragraph with supporting artifacts.
- Mitigations: what was done to stop the impact.
- Action items: owner + due date.
- Artifacts: links to flamegraphs, traces, dashboards, PRs.

Appendix: quick links and where to upload artifacts
- Artifacts root: s3://redwood-artifacts/latency-flares/<incident-id>/
- Template Grafana dashboard: dashboards/Latency-Flare-Hunt.json
- Slack incident channel naming: #inc-flare-<incident-id>

Notes to responders:
- Keep the initial hypothesis simple: runtime fallback vs infra vs traffic shape. One clear hypothesis is better than three weak ones.
- If you need a fast rollback decision, prefer traffic split rollback over global rollback when possible.
- Label collected artifacts with model-version, node-id, and request-shape.

Last updated: 2026-03-10 by Maya Chen

Unresolved questions (working):
- How frequently should the automatic flare collector run without causing noise? 5m window or 60s?
- Should canary and prod sampling rules differ for token-heavy models?
